original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: For one old projector E and the equation R+S+T+U+V=4I-E, classify the rational rank-one solutions that meet target support, and show that every integral solution fails the inherited P-coefficient character.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian native alphabet. This package stays in the abelian symmetric 2-by-2 model and answers the length-6 question left open by the five-call census: five added frames plus one old projector.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the signed-frame escape. Length-6 support exists, but every integral solution fails the inherited character test, so there is no local call-count saving and no selected-frontier change.
stop_rule: Stop after the length-6 support classification for exactly one old projector and the integral character obstruction. Do not census six frames with no old call, and do not add a second old call.
evidence: Exhaustive finite census of the 230300 subset 4-tuples: support holds exactly when three frames are the complementary old projectors and the other two split 2I. Integral splits are {2A,2B} and {2P,2Q}; each detects two calls and four targets. One non-integral pairwise nonparallel witness at t=2 is support only. The inherited determinant, subset-sum necessity, and character inequality are not reproved.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Substantial Cursor Grok assistance with the census, the splitting identity, and the verifier. No independent human or formal-kernel review.

open_questions.question: Can one rational splitting of 2I make the length-6 support solution into a word?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A legal word would lower the eight-call minimum. The integral splittings already fail the P-coefficient test, so only a non-integral splitting could remain.
open_questions.first_step: Apply the inherited P-coefficient character to the displayed t=2 frames (-2/5,4/5,8/5) and (12/5,6/5,-8/5), with old call B and frozen frames A, P, and Q.
open_questions.blocked_by: Support and the first-order character count are necessary, not sufficient. A passing character on t=2 would still not be a word.
